memory_candidates.content: When folding a redundant `description` key into `summary` across an index-entries.json corpus, check per-entry whether `description == summary` before writing any rewrite logic. In this migration, the overwhelming majority of description-bearing entries (filetypes 11/11, latex 10/10, python 6/6, z3 5/5, typst 26/26, most of lean/cslib/nix/web) had description as a byte-identical duplicate of summary, so the fold was a safe plain delete with zero content loss. Only entries where the two diverged (email 8, cslib 5, lean 5) needed an actual authored merge capped at the schema's summary.maxLength, and even fewer of those (13 total) exceeded the cap and needed a genuine rewrite rather than concatenation. Checking dupe-vs-divergent first turns a scary 147-entry editorial task into a mostly-mechanical one with a small, explicitly-enumerated hand-authored subset.

A `path` field in a JSON entry array is not guaranteed unique -- an index-entries.json corpus can legitimately carry two entries sharing one path (e.g. cslib's standards/ci-pipeline.md, one entry per agent variant: cslib-implementation-agent vs. cslib-implementation-hard-agent). A jq transform that targets a specific entry by `.path == "..."` alone will silently apply to both, corrupting the one not intended. Disambiguate by matching on a second, entry-specific field (here, membership in the `load_when.agents` array) before applying a per-entry rewrite.

A plan's corpus-wide invariant check (e.g. 'zero summary fields over 200 chars across all 19 files') can be broader than what the task's own edits could have violated, if pre-existing violations exist in files the task touches for an unrelated reason (here: files edited only to delete a load_when.skills key, never to fold a description, still carried pre-existing over-cap summaries in entries this task never wrote to). When a corpus-wide sweep in a verification phase catches such a case, confirm via a pre-edit backup diff that the violating entries are unchanged by this task's own edits before treating the finding as a regression -- then record it as a documented deviation against the task's *actual* binding verification bar (the one named in the task description) rather than silently fixing unrelated pre-existing content as unplanned scope creep, or silently ignoring a real corpus-wide check.
